bullets: Macro is risk management at scale — the goal is avoiding being on the wrong side of a regime change, not predicting every move.
A regime change that can be named in advance is one that can be positioned for — the rest is just hoping.
The economy functions as a system, not a set of independent levers — pulling one element triggers correlated responses across others.
Back-testing macro calls reveals that misses almost always stem from treating a correlated system as if its parts were independent.
Systems thinking and risk management are the same discipline — the difference lies only in vocabulary, not methodology.
A macro book and a power grid are both systems of correlated risk — they require the same structured approach to manage exposure.
Sustainability risk management and macro risk management follow identical principles — both demand systems-level awareness.
The ability to position for regime changes depends on recognizing that systems evolve, not just that individual variables shift.
